history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this row (seq 2301) is a confirmed duplicate of seq 1006 (id jamalapuram-venkateswara-swamy-temple) — the famous 'Telangana Chinna Tirupati' at Jamalapuram is already fully documented there; keep-or-merge decision needed. Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple at Jamalapuram, Yerrupalem mandal, Khammam district — the most famous Venkateswara temple associated with the Khammam region. Legend holds that sage Jabali Maharshi performed penance at Suchi Gutta and that Lord Venkateswara self-manifested (Swayambhu/Swayam Vyakta) here in response. Renovated by the Vijayanagara emperor Sri Krishnadevaraya, who prayed here en route to Kondapalli fort; a statue of Krishnadevaraya was installed near the temple in 2010 for the 500th anniversary of his coronation. AGE CONFLICT: the Khammam district portal says 'over 1000 years old', the head priest quotes 'more than 850 years', and Chai Bisket says 'over 800 years' — flagged, unverified. Sub-shrines include Padmavathi Ammavaru, Alamelu Ammavaru, Shiva, Ganesh, Ayyappa and Hanuman. CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV town 'Khammam' is wrong — the temple is at Jamalapuram village, ~80-85 km from Khammam town; corrected to Jamalapuram. District (Khammam) and state (Telangana) are correct.

name: Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple (Jamalapuram)
town_description: Jamalapuram is a village in Yerrupalem mandal of Khammam district, Telangana, about 80-85 km from Khammam town and ~52 km from Vijayawada, set among green hills. It is best known for its ancient Swayambhu Venkateswara temple, a major Saturday pilgrimage destination nicknamed 'Telangana Chinna Tirupati'.
